description:
(Summary from jobright.ai; the original posting may say more.)

Human Interest is a fintech company that provides retirement benefits and 401(k) products to small and medium-sized businesses. The Software Engineer I will contribute to building and maintaining scalable, secure software, with a focus on payroll integrations that sync retirement plan data with payroll providers.
Software Engineer I building production fintech software through coding, system design, and data modeling

Responsibilities:
• You will be trusted to work independently and autonomously on your tasks, with ownership of real software deliverables that matter to our customers, product, and business. Our experienced and highly-skilled team will be there to help you as needed
• You’ll get to grow your skills in coding in the context of a large-scale fintech product with a cloud-based service-oriented architecture
• You will get to apply your theoretical knowledge in analyzing software complexity, system design, data modeling, and other topics in a real-life production environment
• You’ll collaborate with highly-skilled software engineers and product experts
• You’ll gain exposure to the culture and software development lifecycle of a fast-moving tech company built on a highly-modern stack

Requirements:
• A Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field, completed
• 0 years of professional experience (excluding internships); this role is well suited to a recent graduate who hasn't yet worked in a tech role outside of an internship
• Completed coursework in applied machine learning (ML) or artificial intelligence (AI)
• Proficient in using AI-powered agentic and non-agentic coding assistants for tasks like analyzing, writing, testing, or debugging software
• Proficiency in at least one modern, industry-standard, object-oriented language (e.g., JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, Kotlin)
• Proficient in building web applications (frontend and backend) on top of common cloud platforms (e.g. AWS)
• Proficient in applying theoretical computer science knowledge (such as data structures and algorithms) in real-life software engineering situations
• Proficient in common practical software engineering skills such as the use of version control, unit testing, and modern editors/IDEs
• This position does not offer sponsorship for work authorization
